| Der Anbieter leitet um oder der Ziel-Origin weicht ab | Verwende im Konnektor den endgültigen dokumentierten API-Origin. Signierte Anfragen folgen keinen Weiterleitungen. |
| Der Anbieter ist nicht verfügbar | Wiederhole den schreibgeschützten Test nach der Wiederherstellung; ersetze einen gültigen Schlüssel nicht allein wegen eines vorübergehenden Ausfalls. |
| Schlüsselrotation | Aktualisiere bei Bedarf die öffentlichen Identitätsfelder, ersetze das Zugangsdatum mit dem privaten Schlüssel und führe dann den schreibgeschützten Test erneut aus. Verwende nie ein zuvor erzeugtes JWT wieder. |

### Agent-Vertrag für signierte JWTs

Ermittle die Vorlage, bevor du einen Konnektor erstellst. Konfiguriere nur öffentliche Felder
unter `config.signed_jwt`. Fordere den privaten Schlüssel über das bestehende sensible
Zugangsdatenformular von SubKit oder die Übergabe an die Browser-Einrichtung an; fordere ihn nicht im Freitext-Chat an
und erzeuge, drucke oder speichere JWTs nicht selbst. Das sichere Formularfeld ist
`private_key`; `token` und OAuth-`client_secret` sind kein Ersatz.

Lies nach dem Speichern das Ergebnis der authentifizierten Probe und melde Anbieterfehler,
ohne Konnektivität zu behaupten. Prüfe den aktuellen Build-/Prüfstatus, bevor du sagst, dass eine
Einladung verwendet werden kann. Eine Einladung oder jede andere Anbieter-Mutation erfordert einen eigenen
autorisierten Workflow; der Einrichtungstest des Konnektors führt nur einen Lesezugriff aus.

Verwende die generierten OpenAPI-Schemas als maschinenlesbaren Vertrag und den an die Vorlage gebundenen
Skill `app-store-connect-basics` für Anbieterhinweise. Die generierten `/llms/setup.md`,
`/llms/connectors.md`, `/llms/cli.md` und `/llms-full.txt` werden mit der Engine ausgeliefert und
aus diesen Quellen neu generiert; pflege keine zweite Auth-Spezifikation.

en.title: Sandbox data tools
en.summary: Which sk helpers JavaScript transforms can use and where their limits are.
en.body:
## Sandbox data tools

JavaScript workflow transforms can use bounded, synchronous `sk` helpers. They
perform no network, filesystem or credential access. Namespaces are immutable.
Promises and unseeded randomness are unsupported; use the execution clock and
`sk.uuid()` for repeatable values.

| Task | Helpers | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decimal amounts | `sk.money.add/sub/mul/div/round/compare` | Decimal strings; `div` and `round` require scale and `down`, `halfUp`, `halfEven` or `up`. No currency conversion. |
| CSV | `sk.csv.parse/stringify` | Explicit delimiter/header options; export escapes spreadsheet formulas by default. Up to 10,000 rows. |
| Dates | `sk.date.parse/format/add/startOf/convertZone` | Date-only values stay dates. Local datetimes require an IANA zone; ambiguous or missing DST times require explicit `earlier`/`later`. |
| Validation | `sk.schema.validate/assert`, `sk.assert` | Local schema references only; no remote resolution or asynchronous validators. |
| URLs | `sk.url.parse/build/query/encode/decode` | WHATWG parsing, repeated query entries, UTF-8 percent encoding. No requests. |
| XML | `sk.xml.parse/build` | Ordered `{name, attributes, children}` trees retain mixed text; no DTD or custom entities. |
| Text and records | `sk.template.render`, `sk.diff.records` | Escaped HTML by default, explicit text mode; bounded list sections. Record diff requires a unique key. |

```javascript
return {
  total: sk.money.add("19.90", "4.95"),
  csv: sk.csv.stringify([{ name: "Ada", amount: "24.85" }]),
  tomorrow: sk.date.add("2024-02-28", 1, "days"),
  greeting: sk.template.render("Hello {{name}}", { name: "Ada" })
};
```

Text inputs and outputs are limited to 1 MiB, structures to 100,000 nodes and
64 levels. Existing sandbox memory, execution and output budgets still apply.
Each helper is embedded and loaded on first access in each sandbox;
regenerate it with `bun run gen:sandbox-tools` and check it with
`bun run check:sandbox-tools-drift`. Package versions and timezone data are pinned
in the lockfile. These tools do not add document rendering, OCR or a browser.
JavaScript transforms, JSONata and binary parsing use bounded worker processes.
The default lane can run two workers in parallel; hooks have a separate lane.
Per-engine-process global and per-tenant queue limits apply across default and
hook workers.
The RSS watchdog is available on Linux; it is a polling limit rather than a
kernel-enforced memory ceiling.

de.title: Sandbox-Datenwerkzeuge
de.summary: Welche sk-Helfer JavaScript-Transformationen nutzen können und wo ihre Grenzen liegen.
de.body:
## Sandbox-Datenwerkzeuge

JavaScript-Workflow-Transformationen können begrenzte, synchrone `sk`-Helfer verwenden. Sie
führen keinen Netzwerk-, Dateisystem- oder Zugangsdatenzugriff aus. Namensräume sind unveränderlich.
Promises und nicht initialisierte Zufallswerte werden nicht unterstützt; verwende die
Ausführungsuhr und `sk.uuid()` für wiederholbare Werte.

| Aufgabe | Helfer | Vertrag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dezimalbeträge | `sk.money.add/sub/mul/div/round/compare` | Dezimalzeichenketten; `div` und `round` erfordern Skalierung und `down`, `halfUp`, `halfEven` oder `up`. Keine Währungsumrechnung. |
| CSV | `sk.csv.parse/stringify` | Explizite Trennzeichen-/Header-Optionen; der Export maskiert Tabellenkalkulationsformeln standardmäßig. Bis zu 10.000 Zeilen. |
| Datum | `sk.date.parse/format/add/startOf/convertZone` | Reine Datumswerte bleiben Daten. Lokale Zeitangaben erfordern eine IANA-Zone; mehrdeutige oder fehlende Sommerzeit-Zeiten erfordern ausdrücklich `earlier`/`later`. |
| Validierung | `sk.schema.validate/assert`, `sk.assert` | Nur lokale Schema-Verweise; keine Auflösung aus der Ferne und keine asynchronen Validatoren. |
| URLs | `sk.url.parse/build/query/encode/decode` | WHATWG-Parsing, wiederholte Query-Einträge, UTF-8-Prozentkodierung. Keine Anfragen. |
| XML | `sk.xml.parse/build` | Geordnete `{name, attributes, children}`-Bäume behalten gemischten Text; kein DTD und keine eigenen Entitäten. |
| Text und Datensätze | `sk.template.render`, `sk.diff.records` | Standardmäßig maskiertes HTML, expliziter Textmodus; begrenzte Listenabschnitte. Der Datensatzvergleich erfordert einen eindeutigen Schlüssel. |

```javascript
return {
  total: sk.money.add("19.90", "4.95"),
  csv: sk.csv.stringify([{ name: "Ada", amount: "24.85" }]),
  tomorrow: sk.date.add("2024-02-28", 1, "days"),
  greeting: sk.template.render("Hello {{name}}", { name: "Ada" })
};
```

Text-Ein- und -Ausgaben sind auf 1 MiB begrenzt, Strukturen auf 100.000 Knoten und 64 Ebenen.
Die bestehenden Sandbox-Budgets für Speicher, Ausführung und Ausgabe gelten weiterhin. Jeder
Helfer ist eingebettet und wird in jeder Sandbox beim ersten Zugriff geladen; generiere ihn
mit `bun run gen:sandbox-tools` neu und prüfe ihn mit `bun run check:sandbox-tools-drift`.
Paketversionen und Zeitzonendaten sind in der Lockfile festgeschrieben. Diese Werkzeuge fügen
weder Dokumenten-Rendering noch OCR noch einen Browser hinzu. JavaScript-Transformationen, JSONata
und Binär-Parsing nutzen begrenzte Worker-Prozesse. Die Standardspur kann zwei Worker parallel
ausführen; Hooks haben eine eigene Spur. Pro Engine-Prozess gelten globale und mandantenbezogene
Warteschlangengrenzen über Standard- und Hook-Worker hinweg. Der RSS-Watchdog ist unter Linux
verfügbar; er ist eine Polling-Grenze und keine vom Kernel durchgesetzte Speicherobergrenze.

en.title: sk CLI reference
en.summary: Every sk command and argument — and the surface authoring runs through: creating or changing a workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill is a definition edit, and definition edits belong here, where the change is a file you can read and a command you can re-run.
en.body:
# sk CLI reference

Every `sk` command and argument — and the surface authoring runs through:
creating or changing a workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill is a
definition edit, and definition edits belong here, where the change is a
file you can read and a command you can re-run.

Running bare `sk` opens the interactive REPL; every command below is
scriptable and prints to stdout. The declarative path — `create --file`,
`update --file`, `validate`, `preview` / `probe` — checks a definition
*before* it exists rather than after, so a mistake costs an error message
instead of a half-built connector someone has to clean up.

The `requires` column is the persona-aware *visibility* gate used for
`--help` filtering — the engine independently enforces permissions on
every API call.

| command | requires | description | subcommands |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `sk agent` | `skill:read` | Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup | `briefing`, `capture`, `init` |
| `sk apikeys` | `api_key:read` | Manage API keys | `create`, `list`, `revoke`, `rotate` |
| `sk apps` | `settings:read` | The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data | `erase-user`, `list`, `show` |
| `sk attach` | `file:write` | Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut) | — |
| `sk audit` | `audit:read` | Query the append-only audit log | `export`, `query`, `show` |
| `sk auth` | `connector:write` | Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route. | — |
| `sk branding` | — | Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding | `get`, `logo`, `reset`, `update` |
| `sk categories` | `workflow:read` | Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind | `list`, `rename` |
| `sk chat` | `chat_workspace:read` | Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack) | `install-space`, `remove-space`, `spaces` |
| `sk clipper` | — | Install the Chrome clipping extension | `install` |
| `sk connector-templates` | `connector:read` | Manage connector templates | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `recipe`, `recipe-pack`, `recipes`, `search`, `set-oauth` |
| `sk connectors` | `connector:read` | Manage connectors | `create`, `delete`, `disable`, `docs-delete`, `docs-ingest`, `docs-list`, `docs-search`, `enable`, `get`, `import`, `inspect`, `list`, `mcp-authorize`, `mcp-inspect`, `patch`, `probe`, `promote`, `test`, `validate` |
| `sk credentials` | `credential:read` | Manage connector credentials | `delete`, `list`, `rotate`, `set` |
| `sk diagnostics` | `audit:read` | Engine diagnostics: errors, LLM status, setup validation | `errors`, `llm`, `setup` |
| `sk discovery` | `discovery:read` | Manage discovery runs and artifacts | `approve`, `artifacts`, `create`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `sk doctor` | — | Diagnose engine connectivity, authentication, and setup. Exits 0 (ok or warn) or 2 (blocked). | — |
| `sk events` | `audit:read` | Query audit events | `get`, `list` |
| `sk executions` | `execution:read` | Manage workflow executions | `abort`, `get`, `list`, `rerun`, `result`, `steps`, `tail` |
| `sk extract` | `conversation:write` | Extract structured data from a file (LLM for text, native parsers for binary) | — |
| `sk files` | `file:read` | Manage files (upload, download, link, …) | `delete`, `download`, `get`, `link`, `list`, `patch`, `stats`, `upload` |
| `sk health` | — | Runtime posture: liveness, token budget, failing runs, risk signals, schema drift, and process runtime. Use `sk doctor` for connectivity/setup. | — |
| `sk hooks` | `inbound_hook:read` | Manage inbound webhook bindings | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list` |
| `sk init` | — | Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot) | — |
| `sk install` | `connector:write` | Guided setup for enterprise integrations | `github`, `google-workspace`, `hubspot`, `jira`, `salesforce`, `slack`, `teams` |
| `sk intake` | `intake:read` | List collected items and start a selected Chat review | `default`, `discard`, `list`, `move`, `restore`, `review` |
| `sk invites` | `identity:read` | Manage user-provisioning invites | `list`, `revoke` |
| `sk join` | — | Redeem an invite to provision your personal API key (no login required) | — |
| `sk knowledge-sources` | `knowledge:read` | Manage knowledge sources | `analyze`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `history`, `import`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `search` |
| `sk login` | — | Authenticate against a subkit engine | — |
| `sk logout` | — | Drop the active profile | — |
| `sk logs` | `audit:read` | Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601. | — |
| `sk ls` | — | List cached conversation sessions for the active profile | — |
| `sk mcp` | — | Run a stdio MCP server proxied to the engine | — |
| `sk notifications` | `notification:read` | Manage notification channels, rules, deliveries, and the inbox | `channels`, `deliveries`, `inbox`, `rules` |
| `sk patch-candidates` | `workflow:read` | Manage patch candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `preview`, `reject` |
| `sk portal-tokens` | `portal_token:read` | Manage portal tokens | `create`, `list`, `revoke` |
| `sk profile` | — | Manage named profiles (environments) | `add`, `delete`, `list`, `show`, `use` |
| `sk rbac` | `rbac:read` | Manage RBAC roles, permissions, grants, groups, and hooks | `can`, `grants`, `groups`, `permissions`, `request-hooks`, `roles`, `users`, `whatcan` |
| `sk rename` | — | Assign or change a short alias for a session (used by `sk -r <alias>`) | — |
| `sk review` | `workflow:read` | Aggregated approval digest: pending patch candidates, proposed skill candidates, and recent failed executions. | — |
| `sk rm` | — | Drop a session from the local cache (the server-side conversation row is preserved) | — |
| `sk schedules` | `workflow:read` | Scheduled workflow runs | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `update` |
| `sk self-healing` | `workflow:write` | Trigger and review proactive drift scans (admin) | `list`, `scan`, `show` |
| `sk sessions` | — | Manage locally-cached conversation sessions | `ls`, `rename`, `rm`, `search`, `show` |
| `sk settings` | `settings:read` | List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked) | `configure`, `get`, `list`, `set` |
| `sk show` | — | Show cached metadata for a session by id or alias | — |
| `sk skill-candidates` | `skill:read` | Manage skill candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `sk skills` | `skill:read` | Manage skills | `activate`, `archive`, `create`, `delete`, `edit`, `get`, `history`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `sync` |
| `sk stats` | `stats:read` | Tenant-scoped runtime statistics (needs stats:read) | `chat`, `connectors`, `conversations`, `events`, `executions`, `http`, `llm`, `mcp`, `operations` |
| `sk status` | — | Print the active profile + engine reachability | — |
| `sk subscriptions` | `subscription:read` | Manage event subscriptions | `create`, `delete`, `deliveries`, `get`, `list`, `patch`, `replay` |
| `sk system` | `system:restart` | Engine process operations (restart) | `restart` |
| `sk system-accounts` | `identity:read` | Manage system accounts | `create`, `delete`, `list` |
| `sk tenants` | — | List tenants you belong to or switch the active one | — |
| `sk update` | — | Update sk CLI to the latest version | — |
| `sk users` | `identity:read` | Manage identity users | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `invite`, `list`, `patch` |
| `sk workflows` | `workflow:read` | Manage workflows | `create`, `delete`, `dry-run`, `get`, `history`, `invoke-snippet`, `list`, `patch`, `preview`, `restore`, `run`, `update`, `validate` |

## Commands and arguments

Every argument of every command. `<name>` is positional; `--name` is a flag.

### `sk agent`

Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup

#### `sk agent briefing`

Print or verify the domain-scoped session briefing for coding agents

- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo; without hooks, else the known domains the repository name names)
- `--budget` (string) — Token budget for the briefing
- `--hook` (default: false) — Hook mode for Codex and Claude Code: inject a repository briefing and show a non-blocking status or warning
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent capture`

Send a session transcript to the engine to collect learnings for review

- `--transcript` (string) — Path to the transcript file (JSONL or text)
- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo)
- `--agent` (string, default: claude-code) — Producing agent name
- `--session-id` (string) — Session id for evidence attribution
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionEnd/Stop-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--detach` (default: false) — Process the hook payload in a detached process
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent init`

Set up automatic SubKit briefings for this repository in Claude Code and Codex

- `--domains` (string, required) — Comma-separated domains for this repository (e.g. accounting, blog-de)
- `--budget` (string) — Optional token budget for each briefing
- `--skip-claude` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json
- `--skip-codex` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.codex/hooks.json


### `sk apikeys`

Manage API keys

#### `sk apikeys create`

Issue a new API key (shown once)

- `--name` (string) — Friendly key name (label)
- `--expires` (string) — Expiry — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (e.g. "workflow:read,workflow:run"). Defaults to your own credential's scopes; ["*"] (full role-derived access, and read-and-execute over MCP) only when your credential has no scope limits. Add "mcp:authoring" for a key that may also author definitions over MCP (a coding agent); leave it off for a key going into a browser client.
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".

#### `sk apikeys list`

List API keys

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk apikeys revoke`

Revoke an API key

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id

#### `sk subscriptions deliveries`

Show deliveries for a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id

#### `sk subscriptions get`

Get a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id

#### `sk subscriptions list`

List subscriptions

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk subscriptions patch`

Update a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id
- `--active` (string, required) — Set active state (true|false)

#### `sk subscriptions replay`

Replay a subscription delivery

- `<sub-id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id
- `<delivery-id>` (positional, required) — Delivery id


### `sk system`

Engine process operations (restart)

#### `sk system restart`

Restart the engine so a saved restart-sensitive setting takes effect (needs a supervisor)

- `--wait` — Wait (up to 240 s) until the restarted engine runs the saved settings
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk system-accounts`

Manage system accounts

#### `sk system-accounts create`

Create a system account

- `--name` (string, required) — Account name

#### `sk system-accounts delete`

Delete a system account

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Account id

#### `sk system-accounts list`

List system accounts

- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk tenants`

List tenants you belong to or switch the active one

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (Bearer)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.sk/config.json)
- `<use>` (positional) — Tenant id to switch to


### `sk update`

Update sk CLI to the latest version

- `--force` (default: false) — Force re-download even if already up to date
- `--check` (default: false) — Check for updates without installing
- `--channel` (string, default: stable) — Release channel: stable | beta
- `--rollback` (default: false) — Restore the most recent retained sk binary
- `--to` (string) — With --rollback, the explicit version to restore (default: most recent retained)


### `sk users`

Manage identity users

#### `sk users create`

Create a user in the caller's tenant

- `--email` (string, required) — User email
- `--role` (string) — Role: admin|member|enduser (default member)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk users delete`

Delete a user

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `sk users get`

Fetch a user by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `sk users invite`

Issue a single-use provisioning invite for a user (token shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id to invite
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (default: your own credential's scopes; ["*"] only when your credential has no scope limits)
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs
- `--ttl` (string) — Invite lifetime in minutes
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk users list`

List identity users

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--app` (string) — Only users who signed in to this app (product_id, see sk apps list)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk users patch`

Update a user's role (admin only)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id
- `--role` (string, required) — New role: admin|member|enduser


### `sk workflows`

Manage workflows

#### `sk workflows create`

Create a workflow from a JSON file (--file) or a solution recipe (--from-recipe <slug>, see `sk connector-templates recipe-pack solutions`). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--file` (string) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--from-recipe` (string) — Slug of a solution recipe; its connectors are bound to the ones you already have
- `--bind` (string) — With --from-recipe: bind connectors yourself, as <template or placeholder>=<connector id or slug>[,…]; needed for templates without a fixed address such as http
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run. With --from-recipe it defaults to the recipe's sample input.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk workflows delete`

Delete a workflow

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `sk workflows dry-run`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)

#### `sk workflows get`

Get a workflow by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `sk workflows history`

List committed versions of a workflow

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk workflows invoke-snippet`

Emit a ready-to-paste, authenticated snippet to run a saved workflow from your own app or CI (curl/node/python).

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--lang` (string, default: curl) — Snippet language: curl (default), node, or python
- `--environment` (string, default: prod) — Where the call runs: prod (default) or dev. Printed as the x-subkit-environment header.
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk workflows list`

List workflows, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--connector` (string) — Only workflows using this connector (id or slug)
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk workflows patch`

Change a workflow's name, description or category without saving a new version (the slug and its wf_<slug> tool stay as they are).

- `<workflow>` (positional, required) — Workflow id or slug
- `--name` (string) — New display name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `sk categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk workflows preview`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)

#### `sk workflows restore`

Restore a prior workflow version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `<version>` (positional, required) — Version number

#### `sk workflows run`

Run a saved workflow, an inline draft definition, or a single step

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id or slug (omit when using --draft or --step)
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string. Prefix with `@` to read from a file (e.g. `--input @./payload.json`).
- `--input-file` (string) — Upload a file and substitute its ref into --input at key K. Format: K=<path>. Repeatable.
- `--draft` (string) — Path to a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (no commit)
- `--step` (string) — Path to a single StepDef JSON file (no workflow persistence)
- `--name` (string) — Optional label for --draft runs (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--slug` (string) — Optional workflow_slug for --step runs (cosmetic)
- `--follow` — Queue the run and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines). Saved workflows only.
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Make this trigger safe to repeat: a second run with the same key is not started, the first run's id comes back instead. Saved workflows only.

#### `sk workflows update`

Update a workflow from a JSON file (PUT the full definition). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass. An unchanged definition does not rotate a version.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--file` (string, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk workflows validate`

Validate a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (structural + step schema checks). No execution, no persistence.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON

de.title: sk-CLI-Referenz
de.summary: Schlag jeden Befehl und jedes Argument der sk-CLI nach.
de.body:
Jeder Befehl und jedes Argument der sk-CLI sowie die Oberfläche, über die das Erstellen läuft: Das Anlegen oder Ändern eines Workflows, Konnektors, einer Knowledge Source oder eines Skills ist eine Definitionsänderung. Die Befehlsreferenz unten wird aus der CLI generiert und bleibt auf Englisch.

# sk CLI reference

Every `sk` command and argument — and the surface authoring runs through:
creating or changing a workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill is a
definition edit, and definition edits belong here, where the change is a
file you can read and a command you can re-run.

Running bare `sk` opens the interactive REPL; every command below is
scriptable and prints to stdout. The declarative path — `create --file`,
`update --file`, `validate`, `preview` / `probe` — checks a definition
*before* it exists rather than after, so a mistake costs an error message
instead of a half-built connector someone has to clean up.

The `requires` column is the persona-aware *visibility* gate used for
`--help` filtering — the engine independently enforces permissions on
every API call.

| command | requires | description | subcommands |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `sk agent` | `skill:read` | Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup | `briefing`, `capture`, `init` |
| `sk apikeys` | `api_key:read` | Manage API keys | `create`, `list`, `revoke`, `rotate` |
| `sk apps` | `settings:read` | The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data | `erase-user`, `list`, `show` |
| `sk attach` | `file:write` | Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut) | — |
| `sk audit` | `audit:read` | Query the append-only audit log | `export`, `query`, `show` |
| `sk auth` | `connector:write` | Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route. | — |
| `sk branding` | — | Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding | `get`, `logo`, `reset`, `update` |
| `sk categories` | `workflow:read` | Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind | `list`, `rename` |
| `sk chat` | `chat_workspace:read` | Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack) | `install-space`, `remove-space`, `spaces` |
| `sk clipper` | — | Install the Chrome clipping extension | `install` |
| `sk connector-templates` | `connector:read` | Manage connector templates | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `recipe`, `recipe-pack`, `recipes`, `search`, `set-oauth` |
| `sk connectors` | `connector:read` | Manage connectors | `create`, `delete`, `disable`, `docs-delete`, `docs-ingest`, `docs-list`, `docs-search`, `enable`, `get`, `import`, `inspect`, `list`, `mcp-authorize`, `mcp-inspect`, `patch`, `probe`, `promote`, `test`, `validate` |
| `sk credentials` | `credential:read` | Manage connector credentials | `delete`, `list`, `rotate`, `set` |
| `sk diagnostics` | `audit:read` | Engine diagnostics: errors, LLM status, setup validation | `errors`, `llm`, `setup` |
| `sk discovery` | `discovery:read` | Manage discovery runs and artifacts | `approve`, `artifacts`, `create`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `sk doctor` | — | Diagnose engine connectivity, authentication, and setup. Exits 0 (ok or warn) or 2 (blocked). | — |
| `sk events` | `audit:read` | Query audit events | `get`, `list` |
| `sk executions` | `execution:read` | Manage workflow executions | `abort`, `get`, `list`, `rerun`, `result`, `steps`, `tail` |
| `sk extract` | `conversation:write` | Extract structured data from a file (LLM for text, native parsers for binary) | — |
| `sk files` | `file:read` | Manage files (upload, download, link, …) | `delete`, `download`, `get`, `link`, `list`, `patch`, `stats`, `upload` |
| `sk health` | — | Runtime posture: liveness, token budget, failing runs, risk signals, schema drift, and process runtime. Use `sk doctor` for connectivity/setup. | — |
| `sk hooks` | `inbound_hook:read` | Manage inbound webhook bindings | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list` |
| `sk init` | — | Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot) | — |
| `sk install` | `connector:write` | Guided setup for enterprise integrations | `github`, `google-workspace`, `hubspot`, `jira`, `salesforce`, `slack`, `teams` |
| `sk intake` | `intake:read` | List collected items and start a selected Chat review | `default`, `discard`, `list`, `move`, `restore`, `review` |
| `sk invites` | `identity:read` | Manage user-provisioning invites | `list`, `revoke` |
| `sk join` | — | Redeem an invite to provision your personal API key (no login required) | — |
| `sk knowledge-sources` | `knowledge:read` | Manage knowledge sources | `analyze`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `history`, `import`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `search` |
| `sk login` | — | Authenticate against a subkit engine | — |
| `sk logout` | — | Drop the active profile | — |
| `sk logs` | `audit:read` | Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601. | — |
| `sk ls` | — | List cached conversation sessions for the active profile | — |
| `sk mcp` | — | Run a stdio MCP server proxied to the engine | — |
| `sk notifications` | `notification:read` | Manage notification channels, rules, deliveries, and the inbox | `channels`, `deliveries`, `inbox`, `rules` |
| `sk patch-candidates` | `workflow:read` | Manage patch candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `preview`, `reject` |
| `sk portal-tokens` | `portal_token:read` | Manage portal tokens | `create`, `list`, `revoke` |
| `sk profile` | — | Manage named profiles (environments) | `add`, `delete`, `list`, `show`, `use` |
| `sk rbac` | `rbac:read` | Manage RBAC roles, permissions, grants, groups, and hooks | `can`, `grants`, `groups`, `permissions`, `request-hooks`, `roles`, `users`, `whatcan` |
| `sk rename` | — | Assign or change a short alias for a session (used by `sk -r <alias>`) | — |
| `sk review` | `workflow:read` | Aggregated approval digest: pending patch candidates, proposed skill candidates, and recent failed executions. | — |
| `sk rm` | — | Drop a session from the local cache (the server-side conversation row is preserved) | — |
| `sk schedules` | `workflow:read` | Scheduled workflow runs | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `update` |
| `sk self-healing` | `workflow:write` | Trigger and review proactive drift scans (admin) | `list`, `scan`, `show` |
| `sk sessions` | — | Manage locally-cached conversation sessions | `ls`, `rename`, `rm`, `search`, `show` |
| `sk settings` | `settings:read` | List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked) | `configure`, `get`, `list`, `set` |
| `sk show` | — | Show cached metadata for a session by id or alias | — |
| `sk skill-candidates` | `skill:read` | Manage skill candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `sk skills` | `skill:read` | Manage skills | `activate`, `archive`, `create`, `delete`, `edit`, `get`, `history`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `sync` |
| `sk stats` | `stats:read` | Tenant-scoped runtime statistics (needs stats:read) | `chat`, `connectors`, `conversations`, `events`, `executions`, `http`, `llm`, `mcp`, `operations` |
| `sk status` | — | Print the active profile + engine reachability | — |
| `sk subscriptions` | `subscription:read` | Manage event subscriptions | `create`, `delete`, `deliveries`, `get`, `list`, `patch`, `replay` |
| `sk system` | `system:restart` | Engine process operations (restart) | `restart` |
| `sk system-accounts` | `identity:read` | Manage system accounts | `create`, `delete`, `list` |
| `sk tenants` | — | List tenants you belong to or switch the active one | — |
| `sk update` | — | Update sk CLI to the latest version | — |
| `sk users` | `identity:read` | Manage identity users | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `invite`, `list`, `patch` |
| `sk workflows` | `workflow:read` | Manage workflows | `create`, `delete`, `dry-run`, `get`, `history`, `invoke-snippet`, `list`, `patch`, `preview`, `restore`, `run`, `update`, `validate` |

## Commands and arguments

Every argument of every command. `<name>` is positional; `--name` is a flag.

### `sk agent`

Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup

#### `sk agent briefing`

Print or verify the domain-scoped session briefing for coding agents

- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo; without hooks, else the known domains the repository name names)
- `--budget` (string) — Token budget for the briefing
- `--hook` (default: false) — Hook mode for Codex and Claude Code: inject a repository briefing and show a non-blocking status or warning
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent capture`

Send a session transcript to the engine to collect learnings for review

- `--transcript` (string) — Path to the transcript file (JSONL or text)
- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo)
- `--agent` (string, default: claude-code) — Producing agent name
- `--session-id` (string) — Session id for evidence attribution
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionEnd/Stop-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--detach` (default: false) — Process the hook payload in a detached process
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent init`

Set up automatic SubKit briefings for this repository in Claude Code and Codex

- `--domains` (string, required) — Comma-separated domains for this repository (e.g. accounting, blog-de)
- `--budget` (string) — Optional token budget for each briefing
- `--skip-claude` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json
- `--skip-codex` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.codex/hooks.json


### `sk apikeys`

Manage API keys

#### `sk apikeys create`

Issue a new API key (shown once)

- `--name` (string) — Friendly key name (label)
- `--expires` (string) — Expiry — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (e.g. "workflow:read,workflow:run"). Defaults to your own credential's scopes; ["*"] (full role-derived access, and read-and-execute over MCP) only when your credential has no scope limits. Add "mcp:authoring" for a key that may also author definitions over MCP (a coding agent); leave it off for a key going into a browser client.
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".

#### `sk apikeys list`

List API keys

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk apikeys revoke`

Revoke an API key

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id

#### `sk apikeys rotate`

Rotate an API key (new key shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id


### `sk apps`

The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data

#### `sk apps erase-user`

Erase an app user: removes SubKit's own data about that person for this app; the account at the sign-in provider stays. Irreversible

- `<app>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `<user>` (positional, required) — User id (listed by sk apps show <app>)
- `--yes` (default: false) — Confirm the erasure without asking
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk apps list`

List the apps of this workspace with environment, users, budget today and readiness

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk apps show`

Show one app: settings, sign-in, workflows, users, today's budget and readiness with the next action

- `<id>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `sk attach`

Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut)

- `<conversation-id>` (positional, required) — Conversation id (UUID)
- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `sk audit`

Query the append-only audit log

#### `sk audit export`

Stream audit log as NDJSON to stdout or a file

- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--output` (string) — Output file path (default: stdout)

#### `sk audit query`

Filter the audit log

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp or relative (e.g. 10m, 1h, 7d)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Filter by resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--cursor` (string) — Continue after a previous page (its next_cursor)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk audit show`

Fetch one audit event by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Audit event id


### `sk auth`

Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route.

- `--connector-id` (string, required) — Connector to reauthenticate
- `--json` — Emit the full response as JSON


### `sk branding`

Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding

#### `sk branding get`

Read tenant branding

- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `sk branding logo`

Download normalized branding logo PNG

- `<theme>` (positional, required) — light or dark
- `--output` (string) — Output file, defaults to stdout
- `--revision` (string)
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `sk branding reset`

Reset branding at an expected revision

- `<revision>` (positional, required)
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `sk branding update`

Replace branding from canonical JSON body (file or - for stdin)

- `<input>` (positional, required) — JSON file or -
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`


### `sk categories`

Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind

#### `sk categories list`

List the catalog categories with how many workflows, connectors, knowledge sources, skills and files use each

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk categories rename`

Rename across all kinds with revision checks; preserve purpose ownership and merge into an existing target

- `<from>` (positional, required) — Current category
- `<to>` (positional, required) — New category
- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk chat`

Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack)

#### `sk chat install-space`

Register a chat space with the engine (Google Chat / Slack)

- `<platform>` (positional) — google_chat | slack
- `<workspace_id>` (positional) — Native space id, e.g. spaces/<id> (Slack: team id T…)
- `--bot-token` (string) — Slack bot token (xoxb-…) — required for slack
- `--default-channel` (string) — Optional default channel
- `--as` (string) — Installer platform user id (auto-filled from a pending space when omitted)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `<version>` (positional, required) — Version number

#### `sk workflows run`

Run a saved workflow, an inline draft definition, or a single step

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id or slug (omit when using --draft or --step)
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string. Prefix with `@` to read from a file (e.g. `--input @./payload.json`).
- `--input-file` (string) — Upload a file and substitute its ref into --input at key K. Format: K=<path>. Repeatable.
- `--draft` (string) — Path to a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (no commit)
- `--step` (string) — Path to a single StepDef JSON file (no workflow persistence)
- `--name` (string) — Optional label for --draft runs (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--slug` (string) — Optional workflow_slug for --step runs (cosmetic)
- `--follow` — Queue the run and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines). Saved workflows only.
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Make this trigger safe to repeat: a second run with the same key is not started, the first run's id comes back instead. Saved workflows only.

#### `sk workflows update`

Update a workflow from a JSON file (PUT the full definition). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass. An unchanged definition does not rotate a version.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--file` (string, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk workflows validate`

Validate a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (structural + step schema checks). No execution, no persistence.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON

en.body:
# subkit runtime settings

Every value below lives in canonical runtime configuration and is editable via
the Cockpit, HTTP/MCP settings APIs, `sk settings configure`, or `sk settings set`. Per-tenant
overrides go into the file's `tenants` section and only honor leaves
tagged `scope=tenant`.

Path resolution: tenant overlay → global value → schema default. Environment
variables never set a runtime setting.

## log
Logging

| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |

## Authentication providers

`auth.providers` is one atomic, validated runtime setting available through Cockpit, HTTP, MCP, `sk settings`, and the canonical config file. Records use `protocol: api_key` or `oidc`; one API-key adapter and multiple named direct OIDC adapters may coexist. Provider ids must be unique, and every OIDC callback is `/v1/identity/login/callback` on `server.public_base_url`. A successful write is active for subsequent browser-login requests without an engine restart.

OIDC records are public clients using Authorization Code with PKCE. Runtime configuration intentionally has no `client_secret` field and rejects one if supplied; use an issuer that supports public clients with `token_endpoint_auth_method=none`. The environment is not an auth-provider source.

Configured labels are diagnostic metadata only. The common `mcp-auth` surface derives its two user actions from protocol and always presents `Continue with SSO` before `Continue with API key`. Discovery exposes the canonical labels `SSO` and `API key`; no provider-specific route or parallel configuration tree is accepted.

Every value below lives in canonical runtime configuration and is editable via
the Cockpit, HTTP/MCP settings APIs, `sk settings configure`, or `sk settings set`. Per-tenant

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `products` | json | `—` | global | no | no | Product settings keyed by product_id for product principals (oidc_bearer providers) |

## Authentication providers

`auth.providers` is one atomic, validated runtime setting available through Cockpit, HTTP, MCP, `sk settings`, and the canonical config file. Records use `protocol: api_key` or `oidc`; one API-key adapter and multiple named direct OIDC adapters may coexist. Provider ids must be unique, and every OIDC callback is `/v1/identity/login/callback` on `server.public_base_url`. A successful write is active for subsequent browser-login requests without an engine restart.

OIDC records are public clients using Authorization Code with PKCE. Runtime configuration intentionally has no `client_secret` field and rejects one if supplied; use an issuer that supports public clients with `token_endpoint_auth_method=none`. The environment is not an auth-provider source.

Configured labels are diagnostic metadata only. The common `mcp-auth` surface derives its two user actions from protocol and always presents `Continue with SSO` before `Continue with API key`. Discovery exposes the canonical labels `SSO` and `API key`; no provider-specific route or parallel configuration tree is accepted.

en.title: Connector & recipe catalog
en.summary: What ships in the box: 61 connector templates across 16 categories, carrying 248 recipes — pre-authored, runnable workflows you clone instead of starting from a blank page.
en.body:
# Connector & recipe catalog

What ships in the box: **61 connector templates** across **16 categories**, carrying **248 recipes** — pre-authored, runnable workflows you clone instead of starting from a blank page.

A **template** connects a system: base URL, auth flow, endpoint schema, and a vendor-basics Skill. A **recipe** is a complete workflow shipped on that template — say what you want in a conversation and sk clones the closest recipe as your starting draft.

# Connector & recipe catalog

What ships in the box: **61 connector templates** across **16 categories**, carrying **248 recipes** — pre-authored, runnable workflows you clone instead of starting from a blank page.

A **template** connects a system: base URL, auth flow, endpoint schema, and a vendor-basics Skill. A **recipe** is a complete workflow shipped on that template — say what you want in a conversation and sk clones the closest recipe as your starting draft.
